content:
Alice Chen: Heads-up — AcmePay reported that their quantized endpoint is slower than FP16 after the 4-bit rollout yesterday. P95 jumped from ~120ms to ~170ms.
Marco Díaz: Ack. Which model and deployment?
Alice Chen: redwood-4bit-1.0 on dedicated pool eu-west-1a, 8-GPU. Customer says tail latency spike on short prompts (~32 tokens).
Priya Kapoor: Short prompts? That's suspicious — batching heuristics should favor throughput but we shouldn't see p95 regressions for small seq lengths. Any KV cache usage?
Alice Chen: They enabled server-side KV caching. I also see increased CPU on the workers around the same time in their logs.
Jordan Lee: Pasting quick profile from one affected inferencer (sanitized):
```
PROFILE SUMMARY
model: redwood-4bit-1.0
input_len: 32
kv_cache: enabled
kernel_select: quant_matmul_4bit (auto)
wall_time_ms: 182.4
- kernel compute: 90.1ms
- encode/decode memcpy: 55.2ms
- quant/dequant overhead: 26.4ms
- batching wait: 10.7ms
```
Marco Díaz: That quant/dequant overhead looks large. Are we doing quantization at runtime for KV segments?
Jordan Lee: Yes — on that runtime path we were applying a per-request calibration for cached KV shards when sequence length widens; it causes an extra copy+re-quant step. Looks like the calibration heuristic kicked in after new traffic pattern.
Priya Kapoor: Repro steps for us?
Alice Chen: I can reproduce locally by sending 1 request every 150ms with seq len 32, KV enabled, model=redwood-4bit-1.0, using the same runtime config as customer. Curl below: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.test/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-4bit-1.0","input":"hello","max_tokens":32,"kv_cache":true}'
```
Jordan Lee: When I force kernel selection to fp16_matmul for that model the P95 drops back to ~125ms and quant/dequant overhead disappears. So kernel routing is picking a 4-bit path that has higher mem-copy cost for small seqs.
Marco Díaz: Why would routing prefer the 4-bit kernel? The decision logic tries to maximize throughput. Maybe it estimated compute win but ignored memcpy and calibration cost.
Priya Kapoor: Right, our kernel scoring is compute-only for quant kernels. For small seq lengths the memory copy and quantization fixed cost dominates. We should adjust scoring to include an estimated memcopy+calibration constant and have a seq_len breakpoint.
Alice Chen: Customer asks for quick mitigation — can we toggle their deployment to prefer FP16 kernels until we ship a fix?
Jordan Lee: Yes, we can set model-variant override -> prefer_fp16_kernels on their deployment. Ops-bot: I created change request CR-4821 to add per-deployment kernel_preference flag.
ops-bot: Change request CR-4821 filed by Jordan Lee.
Priya Kapoor: Short-term patch plan: 1) Add a fast path in kernel selector: if seq_len < 64 and kv_cache enabled and kernel==quant_4bit then prefer fp16. 2) Add a telemetry metric for quantization overhead (quant_dequant_ms). 3) Queue a perf test using our canary rig to validate.
Marco Díaz: Agree. Also add a config knob to disable calibration heuristic per-deployment. That avoids re-quant for cached shards.
Alice Chen: Customer comms: I'll tell AcmePay we can flip them to FP16-pref and that our eng team has a targeted fix ETA ~48 hours and a permanent update in next week's runtime patch.
Priya Kapoor: Can someone attach the profiling trace to the issue? I want to correlate with kernel microbenchmarks.
Jordan Lee: Attached profiling snippet to CR-4821 and pushed microbenchmarks for quant_matmul_4bit vs fp16_matmul (small seqs). Results show 4-bit only wins after seq>=128 or batch>=4.
Marco Díaz: Nice. For longer term we should: a) integrate memory-copy cost into kernel scoring, b) refine calibration frequency (avoid per-request when KV stable), c) add A/B canary for kernel selector changes.
Alice Chen: For the immediate customer fix I'm going to flip their deployment to FP16-pref and schedule a maintenance window to apply the runtime toggle. Priya/Jordan — can you prepare a rollback plan if FP16 causes unexpected cost spikes?
Priya Kapoor: Yup. We'll keep telemetry and a spend alert. If we see >20% token-cost increase across 1h we rollback to quantized route.
support-bot: Noted. Message template for AcmePay: "We've identified a kernel routing issue that increases latency for small prompts with KV caching. We can switch your deployment to use FP16-preferred kernels immediately while we deploy a targeted runtime fix. Expected ETA: 48 hours for hotfix; full fix in next scheduled release."
Alice Chen: I'll send that now. Thanks team.
Jordan Lee: Filing follow-up: add unit tests that simulate KV re-quant path so we don't regress again.
Marco Díaz: Will assign CR-4821 tasks and ETA.
Alice Chen: Closing loop: customer acknowledged and accepted FP16-pref change. I'll update thread after the hotfix verification. :thumbsup:
